A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RDX research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and CUB experiments, ImageNet/iNaturalist model comparisons, numerical BSR evaluations, qualitative explanations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, SemanticLens metric results, and an experiment measuring concept consistency under dataset resampling.

M1.justification: The RDX pipeline retains ranked Euclidean distances, the locally biased difference function, spectral clustering, KNA sampling, and optional CKA alignment. The stated rank range changes from 0–n to 1–n, but this wording correction does not establish a different ranking procedure. The new metrics concern evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same modified MNIST tasks, CUB concept removals, and ImageNet/iNaturalist class groups. The 'Clothes' entry becomes 'Mittens' with identical classes. The new consistency experiment changes sample counts within existing class distributions, rather than adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates top-k sparse autoencoders (TKSAE) and NLMCD, including a comparator explicitly designed for model comparison. Figure 3 replaces its SAE and PCA entries with TKSAE and NLMCD; SAE and PCA remain in appendix evaluations. These additions substantially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds OpenCLIP-based Clarity, Polysemanticity, and modified cross-model Redundancy metrics. Appendix A.5 introduces base/±20% sampling, conversion to hard clusters, and Hungarian matching on 1,200 shared images. These are substantial added evaluation protocols; the original training, dataset splits, and alignment settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 and Figure A11 add a systematic robustness experiment testing whether extracted concepts remain consistent when images are uniformly added or removed. It covers four retained ImageNet subsets and seven methods. Earlier distance-function, sampling, and alignment analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Tables A3–A6 add numerical mean ± summaries beyond v1's boxplots and point-valued tables. However, v2 does not clearly identify the statistic following ± or document additional repeated runs. The previously disclosed global seed remains unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds detailed BSR and SemanticLens results in Tables A3–A6 and consistency findings in Figure A11, where SAE is most consistent and RDX has relatively low disagreement. The reported early MNIST checkpoint accuracy changes from 94% to 95% in Figure 2 and the text, while Table A8 still states 94%; this is an inconsistent reporting revision, not an established performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a formal cross-model adaptation of redundancy: maximum cosine similarity to the other model's concepts, averaged over concepts and symmetrized across directions. Appendix A.5 also defines cluster disagreement after matching. The original RDX mathematical construction is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: RDX explains representational differences, BSR evaluates difference explanations, and experiments recover known and discover unknown differences. The additional evaluations support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of Euclidean versus manifold distances, OpenCLIP evaluator bias, and why isolating differences need not improve clarity or polysemanticity. It also expands the explanation of baseline failures on subtle CUB differences. Most earlier limitations are retained and moved into Section 5.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds concrete TKSAE implementation and training details, including 50 concepts and 200 epochs, plus NLMCD embedding adaptation, cluster selection, and sampling instructions. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures remain. The abstract removes the direct code-repository link while retaining the project-page link; repository availability cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight references, including SemanticLens, NLMCD, k-sparse autoencoders, OpenCLIP, Hungarian matching, and Isomap. NLMCD is incorporated into the discussion of concept-based model comparison. The broader positioning against dictionary learning, representation similarity, and graph comparison remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and caption revisions, clarifies visual concepts, separates the monosemanticity discussion, and moves limitations and societal impact from Appendix A into the main discussion. Appendix material is reorganized, but the central narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The quantitative presentation expands substantially through four detailed comparison tables and a new consistency plot. Figure 3 is redrawn for the revised comparator set, appendix figures are relocated nearer their discussions, and the Yellow Back figure labels are corrected. Most existing qualitative grids and ablation plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation that previously relied mainly on BSR and generic explanation baselines. TKSAE and NLMCD address comparator relevance, additional explanation-quality metrics test complementary properties, and the consistency experiment examines reliability under resampling. These gains improve the evidence supporting RDX while acknowledging its lack of consistent superiority on every metric. Undefined ± summaries and the conflicting 94%/95% checkpoint reports weaken precision but do not outweigh the broader validation.
